page.layout: One page of text, one column; running head at top; page number at top right; signature mark G 3 at the foot; fragments of marginal text at the far left edge of the book (cut off, partly unreadable, not transcribed as notes).

main_text.p: ad basim sunt, angulis, circini cruribus eodem semper intervallo divaricatis: collige jam tres istos arcus, tribus istis angulis subtentos, & in unum arcum dispone: semicirculum habebis, tantam scilicet circuli portionem, quanta duobus rectis angulis subtendendis sufficiat: Eo igitur ventum est, ut tres angulos in triangulo, duobus rectis angulis æquales esse, perinde compertum sit, & experientiâ notum, atque aquam ad frigus se reducere, vel ferrum ad Magnetem tendere. main_text.notes: The left-edge fragments belong to the facing page and are cut off; the word "trian-" at the foot is a line-end hyphenation continuing on the next page. The signature "G 3" is printed at the foot of the page. The page number is printed at the top right as "149".

page.notes: Page number and running head are printed at the top. Partial text at the left edge is from the adjacent page and was not transcribed.
